title: California Code of Civil Procedure section 917.9 - Discretionary undertaking on appeal in other cases
claims: Section 917.9(a) provides that, in cases not provided for in Sections 917.1 to 917.8, the perfecting of an appeal shall not stay enforcement if the trial court in its discretion requires an undertaking and it is not given, where the appellant was found to possess money or other property belonging to the respondent, is required to perform an act for the respondent's benefit, or the judgment is solely for costs awarded under Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 1021) of Title 14.

Section 917.9(b) and (c) provide that the undertaking shall be in a sum fixed by the court, in an amount sufficient to cover all damages the respondent may sustain by reason of the stay in the enforcement of the judgment or order.

Section 917.9(d) defines damages for the purpose of the section as either reasonable compensation for the loss of use of the money or property, or payment of the costs amounts specified in paragraph (3) of subdivision (a).
